### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3fb74b6d30c68f59885773d2428ad1a7dea47147`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **169** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3fb74b6d30c68f59885773d2428ad1a7dea47147` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `667225fd960d138c7511b382f99f2ff242db63ae` — the merge of head `85ec00115a6b5179a99240050a1d9509638e2656` into base `3fb74b6d30c68f59885773d2428ad1a7dea47147`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 667225fd960d138c7511b382f99f2ff242db63ae && git checkout 667225fd960d138c7511b382f99f2ff242db63ae
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3fb74b6d30c68f59885773d2428ad1a7dea47147 85ec00115a6b5179a99240050a1d9509638e2656 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3fb74b6d30c68f59885773d2428ad1a7dea47147 && git merge --no-ff 85ec00115a6b5179a99240050a1d9509638e2656

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3fb74b6d30c68f59885773d2428ad1a7dea47147
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3fb74b6d30c68f59885773d2428ad1a7dea47147` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `85ec00115a6b5179a99240050a1d9509638e2656`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-query-validation.ts (assertSearchFieldsAreSearchable, resolveQueryFields), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-record-reads.ts (the global-search sweep's resolver call), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (narrowStoredMetadataSearch), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (expandSearchOnAst, the find() door ladder), packages/objectql/src/search-filter.ts (fieldClausesForTerm), packages/objectql/src/text-operator-declared-type-door.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-searchable-fields.ts (declaredFieldTarget, checkSearchableFieldList), ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/searchOffer.ts, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx, packages/spec/src/data/masked-field-types.ts, docs/adr/0061-record-search-architecture.md, docs/adr/0049-no-unenforced-security-properties.md, packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.test.ts, packages/rest/src/data-search-field-searchable-flag-door.test.ts, and the shipped object metadata under packages/platform-objects, packages/plugins, packages/services, packages/metadata-core (census of `searchable: true`)

Inputs read: card #29008 body and all six comments (triage 6571567772, director claim 6573084852, ruling 6573569376, exit stroke 6576961902, claim 6577104281, os-dev-report 6578774069); PR #29385 body, 21-file list and the net diff against the merge base `2f7977cd` at the head; the check-runs on the head. The live tree was read with `git show` at the head after `git fetch`; nothing was built, run or re-run.

Gate verdicts on the head at the time of this record: 35 check-runs concluded `success` — among them `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Test Core (8/8)` and seven `Test UI` shards; none concluded `failure`. 19 were still `in_progress`: `Test Core (1–7/8)`, nine `Test UI` shards, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · workspace` (the last carries `check:docs` / `check:api-surface` for the regenerated references and the new export). This record judges the contract and the design on the tree; it does not stand in for those conclusions — the seat lands only once every required context is `success` (in_progress is not a pass).

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged against the live tree:

1. **The auto-default search set widens** (search-fields.ts `autoDefaultFields`): with no `searchableFields`, a field with `searchable === true`, a readable `type` not in `SEARCH_FLAG_EXCLUDED_TYPES` and not virtual joins the set, asked before the system-name / `hidden` / type exclusions. **Right** — this is ruling 6573569376 letter A verbatim ("the type-based auto-default plus every field marked `searchable: true`, of any type, except the hard exclusions"). The declared branch reads no flag — **right**, the ruling keeps a declaration "the whole search set (unchanged)".
2. **The `$searchFields` ingress allow-list widens identically** (protocol-query-validation.ts:928 `assertSearchFieldsAreSearchable` → `resolveSearchFieldResolution({ fields: gate.fields, … })`). Read `resolveQueryFields` (:339): `gate.fields` is the registry's `schema.fields` unprojected, so the flag reaches the gate. **Right**, and the ruling's "`resolveSearchFields` and the #4254 gate stay one source" holds without a `domain:server` edit. The gate's `internal: true` refusal (first) and `credential` refusal (before the source branch) are unchanged and still precede the flag's effect — a flagged `internal` text field is 400 at the door and withheld in the engine; consistent.
3. **The engine's scan set widens identically** (engine.ts:14161 `expandSearchOnAst`): `scanFields` is `schema.fields` minus `collectInternalReadFields` ∪ `collectCredentialFields`, handed to the same resolver, then narrowed by `getQueryableFields` (`withholdUnqueryable`). The field meta is the object's whole field definition (search-filter.ts:146 says so for `multiple`), so `searchable` is read. **Right**. The credential strip is what makes the `secret` / `password` hard exclusion a one-source fact rather than a door/engine disagreement — the set's docblock cites ADR-0100 for this and the engine code confirms it.
4. **The global-search sweep** (protocol-record-reads.ts:495) and **the stored-metadata narrowing** (protocol.ts:5458) both pass the object's full field records to the resolver — **right**, they move with it; no second definition of the set survives (protocol.ts:15192's palette history describes the pre-#7643 reader that was removed, not a live one).
5. **The lint allowed set widens identically**: `declaredFieldTarget` (validate-searchable-fields.ts:259) now carries `searchable: f.searchable === true`; it was the one projection that dropped the flag. **Right**. The system-declared stub `{}` in `resolveAllowedSet` cannot be flagged, so the stub still cannot leak into the auto-default — the module's own invariant holds.
6. **The ui readers** (`searchOffer.ts:53`, `ListView.tsx:1488`) pass the served field meta whole — **right**, they agree with the server without an edit (card step 1 confirms the served schema carries `searchable: true`).
7. **Public surface**: new export `SEARCH_FLAG_EXCLUDED_TYPES` (`@objectstack/spec/data`), new optional `SearchFieldMeta.searchable`; `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` carry the export — **right** (`check:api-surface` reads built `dist`, so the `Type Check · workspace` conclusion is the gate's word). The `.describe()` change regenerates `content/docs/references/data/field.mdx`, `data/object.mdx`, `system/migration.mdx` — **right** per the § Touched `packages/spec` table (`check:docs`). No authorable key is added, so `check:authorable-surface` has nothing to move — **right**.
8. **Refusal wording** at the door (`type 'code'`, `not marked 'searchable: true'`, `Mark the field 'searchable: true', or declare 'searchableFields'…`; hard-excluded types keep the old remedy and say "never scans even when marked") and the lint verdict/hint mirror the resolver's precedence exactly (system name → hidden → type, with `flaggable` computed for every arm). Checked the combinations: flagged+hard-excluded, unflagged system name, hidden+secret, `!meta` — no message offers a remedy the resolver would refuse. **Right**. No runtime string carries a tracker number.
9. **Liveness row** (`liveness/field.json` `searchable`): evidence moved from a dashboard widget's own `searchable` key to `admittedBySearchableFlag` and its three readers — **right**, and `Spec property liveness` concluded `success`.
10. **Shipped metadata census** (read, not reviewed): across `packages/platform-objects`, `packages/plugins`, `packages/services`, `packages/metadata-core`, every `searchable: true` on a field outside the type default is one of seven `lookup`s on six objects that declare no `searchableFields` (`sys_session.user_id`, `sys_activity.actor_id` / `environment_id`, `sys_audit_log.user_id`, `sys_comment.author_id`, `notification_preference.user_id`, `sys_presence.user_id`) — the PR body's census is exact. Every other hit is `text` / `textarea` / `email` / `select` (already in the default) or the object-level `enable.searchable`, which is a different key. So the only platform-side widening is a `$icontains` over seven stored user-id strings — string-capable columns, no driver hazard.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/29008-field-searchable-honoured.md`: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/lint` at `minor`; body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic` at line start, matching the PR body's two lines. **Matches what the diff publishes**: the three packages whose `src` moves are exactly the three listed (rest and objectql move only in tests / not at all); the key's meaning changes from inert to read, which is `semantic`; the rule "a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves" gives `minor` on all three. `Check Changeset` concluded `success`; the dev's offline `check-changeset-no-major` reading (no major, level axis widening/semantic) is consistent with the rule. No BREAKING arm, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed. The "What may now match more" paragraph gives the author the two remedies (remove the flag, or declare `searchableFields`) — the migration note a widening owes.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — the search accept set (auto-default, ingress allow-list, engine scan set, lint allowed set) widens by every flagged non-excluded field; nothing is narrowed, no caller that worked stops working.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev `open_questions` (os-dev-report 6578774069):

- **Q1 — ADR-0061 D2 still says field-level `searchable` "stays pruned"; where does the amendment land?** Answered **A**: the seat files a separate Tier H card on `docs/adr/0061-record-search-architecture.md` (the seat's draft `spec-seat2/29008-adr-0061-note.md`), and this PR stays ungoverned — B would hold a non-governed widening behind a governed approval, and the code is not "quietly doing the opposite" (Prime Directive #13): `search-fields.ts` and the changeset name ruling record 6573569376 as the decision and say D2 predates it. **Escalated to the maintainer / the seat's own queue**: the amendment is owed, not optional — until it lands, D2 and the shipped behaviour contradict, and ADR-0061 D5 ("secret / encrypted / PII never searchable") should be re-read in the same note because the hard exclusions are what keep D5 true under the flag. File it before or at landing; the card is the seat's.
- **Q2 — a flagged `hidden` field or a flagged system-column name joins the set; intended?** Answered **A (as taken)**, and it holds against the tree: `hidden` is "Hidden from default UI" (field.zod.ts:2364), a UI fact, not a security boundary; the security boundaries on `$search` are `internal: true` (engine strip + door refusal), the credential types (engine strip, hard exclusion, door `credential` branch) and `getQueryableFields` (`withholdUnqueryable`), all enforced upstream of or beside the resolver and untouched here. A flagged system-name field (`owner_id`, `id`) is the author's explicit act, the per-field twin of naming it in `searchableFields`, which already bypasses the same three exclusions. Pinned with unflagged controls. No change asked.
- **Q3 — a flagged field whose type can never hold a string (`number`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `time`, `json`, …) joins the set and the engine emits `$icontains` over it; narrow the flag?** **Escalated** — see ④ should-fix 2. Verified on the tree: in `find()` the #15661 door (`assertTextOperatorTargetsAreStringCapable`, engine.ts:1302, run from the filter ladder at :14464-ish on the caller's own `where`) runs BEFORE `expandSearchOnAst` (:14478), so the expansion's clauses are never judged by it and reach the driver; SQLite coerces, Postgres does not (NOT MEASURED, as the dev says). The ruling's "of any type" is explicit, the shape pre-exists for a declared `searchableFields` naming such a column, and the shipped census (① item 10) has no such field — so this is not a FAIL, but it is the one decision the maintainer should take rather than the seat.
- **Q4 — keep the export name `SEARCH_FLAG_EXCLUDED_TYPES`?** Answered **A**: keep. It sits beside `SEARCH_AUTO_EXCLUDED_TYPES` / `SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES`, is pinned to exactly three members and to cover `MASKED_ON_READ_FIELD_TYPES`, and the two refusal faces read it rather than carrying a literal — the one-source posture the file exists for. It is an export name, not a metadata key.

Dev `deviations` and declarations: the lint / door / `os explain` message rewrites and the six `content/docs` pages fall under "made false must be fixed" — accepted (the old sentence "which 'search' cannot scan" is false after this change; the forced test edit is named in the PR body). The three-package `minor` is the rule's own answer (②). `check-dev-prereqs` not green locally for `ui/**` dist — CI's `Type Check UI` is the word, pending at write time. The `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` line (skills/objectstack-data, objectstack-query, objectstack-ui list-views teach the auto-default as type-only) names a Tier H follow-up — the seat's, not this PR's; noted so it is not lost. `out_of_scope_findings` class a (non-text `$icontains` on Postgres, `domain:server`) is the same item as Q3 and carries the escalation; class c (the engine's empty-set refusal names only `searchableFields` as its remedy) is wording, correctly left to the next objectql search PR.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts`** — judged against ruling 6573569376 (A), ADR-0061 D1/D2/D5, ADR-0049 (enforce-or-remove), and its first consumers (the door at protocol-query-validation.ts:928, the engine at engine.ts:14161, the lint rule, the sweep, the ui readers).

- The ruling's three clauses are implemented where the ruling says, in the one resolver every reader shares: declared set whole and flag-blind; auto set = type default ∪ flagged, minus `secret` / `password` / `vector`; the ingress allow-list is the same set because it is the same function over the same registry field map. Verified each consumer passes the flag through (① 2–6). The ablation the dev reports (flag line replaced, 5/50 + 1/73 + 1/4 red, controls green, byte-identical restore) is consistent with the test diff read here; not re-run.
- `admittedBySearchableFlag` fails closed on an unreadable `type` — necessary, because the hard exclusion cannot be judged without it and because the lint's registry-column stubs `{}` must not enter the auto-default. Pinned.
- The extra exclusion beyond the ruling's three — a virtual `formula` — is a storage fact the declared branch already applies (`isVirtualSearchField`), not a taste judgment; admitting it would put a name in the allow-list that no driver has a column for, the exact drift #4254 closed. **Right** to keep it out, and the describe says so.
- Flag-before-exclusions ordering: deliberate, documented at the site, tested with unflagged controls; holds (③ Q2).
- `SEARCH_FLAG_EXCLUDED_TYPES` ⊆ `SEARCH_AUTO_EXCLUDED_TYPES` and ⊇ `MASKED_ON_READ_FIELD_TYPES` are both pinned, so a new credential type cannot become flaggable by drift and the #6934 fail-closed direction still holds.
- Tried to break it: flagged `id` (admitted — explicit act, ③ Q2); flagged `internal: true` text field (engine strips before resolving, door refuses first — never scanned, never accepted); flagged field the caller may not query (`withholdUnqueryable` withholds unless named, then the guard refuses loudly — unchanged); flagged multi-valued `lookup` (`fieldClausesForTerm` emits membership `$contains`, the pre-existing #21009 shape); companion `__search` join rule (reads source fields, not the allowed set — unaffected); `searchable: false` on a `text` field (cannot opt out: the key defaults to `false`, so every parsed field carries it — the design is right, see should-fix 1 for the author-facing text); display-field ordering with a flagged lead (pinned).
- **Should-fix 2 (escalate; not a FAIL)** — a flagged field of a type the #15661 door calls never-string-capable is admitted and its `$icontains` clause bypasses that door (the expansion runs after the door ladder in `find()`, verified at engine.ts:14464–14478). On a Postgres dialect a text operator over an integer / boolean / date column errors, so a tenant whose inert `searchable: true` on a `number` field becomes live at upgrade may lose `$search` on that whole object; on SQLite it coerces and matches on the textual form. Not new in kind (a declared `searchableFields` naming such a column has had this shape since #6674) and no shipped object has one (① 10), but this PR is what turns an inert author key into a live one, which is why the maintainer should choose: (a) narrow `admittedBySearchableFlag` by the spec's own text-operator sets (`filter-text-operator-declared-type.ts`, one predicate plus a test flip — departs from "of any type"), or (b) have the expansion skip or cast non-string-capable columns for both branches (`domain:server`, covers the declared branch too). The dev recommends (b)'s lane; this review agrees it is the better home, and asks that the card be filed before landing so the risk is tracked rather than noted.

**`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`** — judged against the ruling's second clause ("the key's `.describe()` says this sentence instead of 'Is searchable'; the field reference pages are regenerated") and its first consumer, the generated `content/docs/references/data/field.mdx`.

- The describe states the ruling's rule in author terms: when it is read (no `searchableFields`), what it adds (any type except the three), the storage caveat (virtual `formula`), and when it is not read (declared list, ADR-0061). The TSDoc above it names the ruling record and the reader. The reference pages are regenerated (three files, byte-consistent with the describe diff). **Right**.
- **Should-fix 1** — the describe does not say that `false` is the default and does NOT withdraw a field the type default already scans. An author who reads the reference page and writes `searchable: false` on a `text` column to keep it out of `$search` gets no refusal and no effect; the only remedies are declaring `searchableFields` (or `hidden: true`, which also hides the column). The `SearchFieldMeta.searchable` TSDoc says exactly this ("`false` and absent are one answer … it can widen the auto-default and never narrows it"), but that sentence is on the internal type, not on the author-facing key. One clause on the describe ("`false`, the default, does not remove a field the type default scans — declare `searchableFields` to choose the set") and a `gen:docs` regeneration closes it. Not a FAIL: the behaviour is the ruling's and is pinned; only the author's expectation is unaddressed.

No must-fix found. Both should-fixes are on the `hits` files; the second carries the one escalation.
